title: Rapid sequence induction and intubation
regimen: Chains: fentanyl · midazolam · sux  |  fentanyl · propofol · sux  |  ketamine · sux
dagger_note: † = clinical or local addition, not in the SA STG. Any item without a source page is †; items with a page are from the STG.
item_format: steps[].actions[]: n=number, t=action, x=detail, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold. steps[].sequence[]: ordered drug cells (m=a/b/c). steps[].decisions[]: if/then/goto. reference{}: drugs, dose_table, later.

items.t: At risk of aspiration
GCS ≤8 or falling; absent gag; pooling secretions / vomit
Inhalational burn (stridor, soot, hoarse)
Expanding neck haematoma, refractory angioedema
SpO₂ <90% despite NRB / BVM + PEEP / NIV
Hypoxaemic respiratory failure
Hypercapnia with ↓GCS; exhaustion, silent chest
Excessive work of breathing: asthma, COPD, metabolic acidosis, fatigue
Severe TBI; refractory status epilepticus
Combative – needs CT / transfer; major trauma
Brain injury needing PCO₂ / PO₂ control
Trained, experienced medical practitioner only
Difficult intubation anticipated: no muscle relaxant
→ Senior / anaesthetist; Plans B–D open first
Obliterated airway anatomy → surgical airway
Valid DNR / ceiling of care
Upper / lower motor neuron defect; disuse atrophy
Prolonged denervation (ICU >3 days); muscle trauma, tumour, inflammation
Burns; severe infection
Pre-existing hyperkalaemia (AKI/CKD, rhabdo, peaked T)
Malignant hyperthermia
Pseudocholinesterase deficiency; myopathy; family MH; open globe / ↑ICP (caution)
Rocuronium 0.9 mg/kg IV, lasts about 60 min
Long block is a problem if intubation fails

steps.title: PREPARE
steps.subtitle: team, monitors, access, kit, drugs drawn up

actions.x: intubator · assistant · drug nurse · scribe/timer; LEMON; say Plan A–D aloud
SpO₂, ECG, NIBP q2–3 min, EtCO₂
line with fast-running fluids, induction agent given through it; resuscitation medicines and equipment at hand; 2nd IV line †
suction on · O₂ NRB + nasal cannula · ETT 7.0 ♀ / 8.0 ♂ + smaller, stylet, bougie · 2 laryngoscopes · OPA/NPA · iGel 3–5 · BVM + PEEP valve · vent set
a, b, c + flushes, push-dose adrenaline, atropine; FONA kit open (#10 scalpel, bougie, 6.0 ETT)
ramp if obese
NRB 15 L/min + nasal cannula 15 L/min, kept on throughout; target SpO₂ ≥94% (or 8 vital-capacity breaths)

actions.t: Correct haemodynamics: SBP >90 / MAP >65 before drugs
actions.x: shock index (HR/SBP) >0.9 → fluids, reduce doses
1 mg in 100 mL NaCl = 10 mcg/mL; 1–2 mL IV q2–5 min for SBP <90

actions.t: Decompress pneumothorax; empty a distended stomach
actions.x: suction / NGT

decisions.then: BVM with PEEP 5–10 or NIV, then continue

steps.title: GIVE THE DRUGS IN THIS ORDER
steps.subtitle: weigh / estimate kg, say it aloud, read the dose from the table; pick ONE chain

decisions.then: use chain III; etomidate or ketamine preferred, propofol can produce hypotension
doses shown are healthy-adult doses; substantial reductions may be needed

actions.x: no mask ventilation unless SpO₂ <93% (gastric insufflation, aspiration); then gentle 2-hand BVM
30–60 s after suxamethonium
release if view worse †

actions.t: Pass the tube: ≤30 s or SpO₂ <93% → abort and re-oxygenate
actions.x: BURP, head lift, bougie, change blade/operator; max 3 attempts

actions.t: Confirm: sustained EtCO₂ × 6 breaths (no trace = wrong place)
actions.x: tube seen through cords; chest rise, air entry, silent epigastrium; depth ≈ 21 cm ♀ / 23 cm ♂; cuff 20–30 cmH₂O; secure

decisions.if: Failed intubation (3 attempts or cannot oxygenate)
decisions.then: Plan B: SGA (iGel) → Plan C: 2-person BVM + OPA/NPA (sux wears off quickly, spontaneous breathing resumes) → Plan D: CICO, scalpel–bougie–tube cricothyroidotomy

steps.title: SEDATE FIRST, THEN VENTILATE
steps.subtitle: sux wears off in about 5 min: never paralyse without sedation

actions.x: treat pain first; midazolam 0.05 mg/kg bolus †, then infusion 0.05–0.2 mg/kg/h (<24 h); record sedation level
A/C or SIMV; FiO₂ 1.0 · Vt 5–8 mL/kg predicted body weight · RR 12–15 · PEEP 5 · I:E 1:2
FiO₂ ↓0.1 every 10 min to 0.4, SpO₂ ≥95% (≥88% if ARDS); PCO₂ 4.5–6.0 kPa (brain injury 4.2–4.8); pH not below 7.20
ABG, SpO₂, all ventilator parameters; BP q5 min × 30 min then q15; EtCO₂ continuous
OGT/NGT, head-up 30°, IDC, CXR tip 3–5 cm above carina; record time, drugs, CL grade, attempts, ETT size and depth

drugs.name: Suxamethonium
drugs.when: T 0, straight after the induction agent

items.t: ≥72 h: midazolam 0.2 mg/kg/h or lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg/h
Add morphine 0.1–0.2 mg/kg/h or fentanyl 1 mcg/kg/h
Unstable: ketamine 0.5–1 mg/kg/h
Pressure control: 15 cmH₂O above PEEP
Asthma / COPD: I:E 1:3–1:4, RR 10–12; COPD SpO₂ 88–92%
Plateau <30, peak <35 cmH₂O; PBW ♂ 50 / ♀ 45.5 + 0.91 × (ht cm − 152.4)
Displaced · Obstructed · Pneumothorax · Equipment · Stacked breaths / Stomach
Hypotension: fluids, push-dose adrenaline, exclude tension pneumothorax; auto-PEEP → disconnect
ICU / tertiary referral – district level
Repeat sux doses: bradycardia, prolonged block
Atropine 0.5 mg IV
Prolonged apnoea (pseudocholinesterase deficiency): keep sedated & ventilated
Calcium gluconate 10%, 10 mL slow IV over 10 min; repeat if ECG changes persist or recur
Dextrose 50% 100 mL IV, then soluble insulin 10 units IV over 5 min; HGT hourly × 6 h
In arrest: calcium as bolus, continue CPR
Dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg IV once, large-bore cannula, in 60 mL water (70 kg: 175 mg, 9 vials)
Repeat to clinical effect; >10 mg/kg uncommon – question diagnosis
Rising EtCO₂, rigidity, masseter spasm, ↑temp; stop triggers, 100% O₂, cool; ICU referral
